reference_soap.plan: If vision, pupils, and the remainder of the eye examination are normal and there is no significant trauma, provide reassurance and optional artificial tears for comfort; the blood usually clears over 1 to 2 weeks. Check blood pressure and review anticoagulant use when indicated. Arrange prompt assessment for pain, photophobia, reduced vision, significant trauma, recurrent episodes, or other bleeding symptoms.

red_flags: Recurrent episodes would warrant a bleeding disorder or blood pressure workup

must_ask.objective: Confirm painless and no vision change
must_ask.say: Is there any pain, or has your vision changed at all?
Did this happen right after coughing, sneezing, or straining?

must_ask.objective: Screen for blood thinner use or bleeding disorders
must_ask.say: Do you take any blood thinners like aspirin or warfarin, or have any bleeding problems?
With a normal eye examination, this is usually harmless and clears on its own over about one to two weeks. Seek care promptly if you develop pain or vision changes.
